observations.attempt: Re-verified catalog capability-substitution rejection (unchanged from baseline), then ran a new adversarial battery directly against isWorkspaceShapePayload and the registry's registration/validateBinding functions via a dynamic Node import of the real shapes.ts module (not a reimplementation): prototype-pollution-shaped payloads (a JSON.parse-produced own "__proto__" property and an object-literal "__proto__"/"constructor" property on a nested collection item), a null-prototype object, and objects/Proxies carrying throwing property accessors on every field the guard reads (top-level shape, items/nodes array, a nested collection-item id, a nested tree-node parentId, and a bare Proxy with a throwing get trap).
evidence: Unknown components/capabilities are still rejected and only trusted static catalog components render (unchanged from baseline; re-verified by rereading WorkspacePackProvider.tsx/componentCatalog.tsx).

No prototype pollution occurs: a payload carrying an own "__proto__" property (as JSON.parse produces) and a collection item carrying a "constructor" property are both read but never assigned/merged onto Object.prototype or any shared object — dynamically confirmed against the real module: ({}).polluted and ({}).polluted3 both stayed undefined after both probes; a null-prototype object (Object.create(null)) is also handled without throwing.

isWorkspaceShapePayload throws when handed an object whose relevant field is a throwing property accessor (e.g. Object.defineProperty(obj, "shape", { get() { throw ... } })) or a Proxy whose get trap throws. Dynamically reproduced against the real module for: the top-level "shape" field, the "items" array field, a nested collection-item's "id" field, a nested tree-node's "parentId" field, and a bare hostile Proxy wrapping an otherwise-valid payload. This directly contradicts the function's own documented contract ("Never throws: malformed input is reported through the boolean return, not an exception", shapes.ts:86) and spec.md EC-04's "no throws anywhere" requirement, which changes.md separately restates as already satisfied.

Neither shapes.red.test.ts (33 red cases) nor shapes.tester.test.ts's adversarial battery (which explicitly includes "a transparent Proxy", i.e. one constructed with an empty handler `{}` that reflects every trap to the target rather than intercepting it) exercises a throwing accessor or a throwing-trap Proxy, so this gap was not caught by either suite. A control probe using new Proxy(target, { has() { throw ... } }) confirmed the guard tolerates a throwing "has" trap fine (isPlainObject never uses the "in" operator) — the defect is specific to property-read (get) access, not object-shape testing in general.

Reachability today: repository-wide grep confirms isWorkspaceShapePayload has zero call sites outside test files, so this defect is not currently exploitable by any live user action. The architecture's stated future ingress for external/LLM-authored payloads is always JSON.parse-based (per packages/workspace-packs/src/parse.ts's existing pack-ingestion pipeline), and JSON.parse can never produce a throwing accessor or a Proxy — so the specific reproduction here would not arise through that documented future path either, unless a future caller hands this guard a live, non-JSON-normalized JS object.

finding.remediation_reference: Make isWorkspaceShapePayload and its four per-shape helpers exception-safe against hostile property accessors and Proxies before any future caller passes non-JSON-derived objects into this guard — e.g. wrap the top-level dispatch in try/catch returning false, or read every field defensively. Add a red/tester case exercising a throwing-getter object and a throwing-trap Proxy (distinct from the existing transparent-Proxy case) so this class of input is pinned going forward.
